title: Chromatic Aberration Consideration for Optimum Bright Field Imaging Using 4D STEM Data
content: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is widely used for atomic-scale observation of materials, normally employing imaging techniques such as annular dark field (ADF) and annular bright field (ABF) imaging. However, their relatively poor image sensitivity has limited atomic-resolution STEM observation of beam-sensitive materials. Recently, Optimum Bright Field (OBF) imaging has been developed using segmented and pixelated detectors [1,2], enabling high SNR imaging at very low dose condition. OBF reconstructs images using weighting functions theoretically designed for maximizing the SNR under the weak phase object approximation (WPOA). Fig. 1 shows the schematic of OBF reconstruction procedures using a pixelated detector. This reconstruction forms high-SNR images even under low electron dose conditions, making it effective for observing electron-beam-sensitive materials such as zeolites and metal-organic frameworks. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials are representative examples of electron-beam-sensitive materials, the applicability of OBF to 2D materials has not yet been thoroughly explored. Since low accelerating voltages are required for observing 2D materials, chromatic aberration is expected to be a significant issue. In the previous research, the single side band (SSB) ptychography is shown to be affected by chromatic aberration [3].
